registered_before: any change of the probe, loader or worker for a lineage tag
outcome_of_amendment_1: B3 did not meet its registered criterion: the native arm flagged 0/525 control, 0/439 admin and 0/523 benign intervals and known tools were flagged 0/439, but the session model under the registered Gumbel rule detected 0/522 attacks (thresholds 37.7 and 42.4, above every measured score). The decision of amendment 1 stands: a session model is not made an alert path, and no live confirmation of that design is registered. B2 was negative (372/439 still flagged)
what_this_amendment_registers: a narrower step: the lineage tag as telemetry only. The probe marks every thread as native (the workload's own process tree) or session (entered through a runtime exec, and its descendants) and the loader reports, per window, the session share of the gram counts next to the unchanged window. Nothing in the alert path changes: the worker scores the whole window with the lidds-ml-v5 model as before, so the next live run stays comparable with pulse-live-v5-1110
why: the proxy of B3 cannot tell a session gram the workload also knows from a native one, and it cannot say which lineage a real attack inside the service falls in. With the kernel's tag the next live run measures the native stream directly

design.tag: pulse_task_state.lineage, 0 native, 1 session; in the gram key through the pad field
design.assignment: at fork (raw_tp/sched_process_fork) the child takes its parent's tag, so a child cannot change lineage by outliving its parent before its first syscall; a task first seen without a state takes the tag of its thread-group leader, else of its parent when the parent is in the same cgroup, else it is native when its pid in its own pid namespace is 1 (the container's entrypoint) and session otherwise (a runtime exec joins an existing pid namespace from a parent outside the cgroup)
design.known_limits: a pod with a shared process namespace (none in the production namespace on 13/11); a session process orphaned before the probe attached is taken as native

proof_before_any_run: the existing token proof (one token per syscall, counts equal) must still pass with the tag; added checks on one worker: a kubectl exec process and its child are counted as session, the container's own threads as native, and the sum of both lineages equals the window that the untagged build reports

hypotheses_for_the_next_live_run.H1: the native stream alone, scored with the lidds-ml-v5 workload model and threshold, flags at most 5 % of the admin-command and benign-binary intervals
hypotheses_for_the_next_live_run.H2: attacks that run inside the workload's own process tree (LID-DS scenarios replayed on the cluster, in-process fixtures) are detected on the native stream at the registered level (recall >= 95 %)
hypotheses_for_the_next_live_run.note: the run's own protocol fixes trials, sample sizes and the handling of the session stream before it starts; exec probes of the kubelet belong to the session stream and are reported

lidds: LID-DS 2021 recordings contain no runtime exec, every event is native: the registered result is unchanged by construction; the offline scorer is not touched
